title: The one-object story
summary: A free 10-minute speaking activity for early speakers and a parent or partner. Choose an object, tell a moment, listen and try one change.
introduction: A familiar object. One real moment. A listener who helps you find the next step.

steps.title: Choose one object
steps.detail: Pick something familiar: a pencil, a toy, a book or a small keepsake. Tell your listener why you chose it.

steps.title: Find one moment
steps.detail: Think of a time you used it, found it or shared it. What happened? Choose one detail your listener could picture.

steps.title: Tell the story
steps.detail: Name the object, tell the moment and finish with why it matters. Aim for 30–60 seconds. A shorter attempt is fine.

steps.title: Listen for one thing
steps.detail: The listener names one clear detail, then asks one useful question. Choose a single change to try.

steps.title: Try it again
steps.detail: Retell the story with that change. Talk about what became clearer. Finish with something the speaker wants to try next time.

listenerGuide: Give them time to finish. Name something specific you understood, then ask one question.
feedbackExample: I could picture the bright blue cover. What happened when you opened the book?
editorialNote: Original illustrative practice activity introduced in flagship V05. No student information or outcome claims.
